falling-asleep-without-pills.title: Falling asleep without pills or dread
falling-asleep-without-pills.line: I go to bed expecting to sleep, and most nights I do.
falling-asleep-without-pills.writerNotes: The copy guide's own after-example. HABIT shows four nurse sessions beat the leaflet for 12 months; NICE judged Sleepio better than pills. Outcome is the relief, not the therapy.

insomnia-help-on-my-phone.title: Insomnia therapy I can follow on my own phone
insomnia-help-on-my-phone.line: I work through a few weeks of sleep lessons and a sleep diary on my phone, at my own pace, without a waiting list.
insomnia-help-on-my-phone.writerNotes: Sleepio (six weeks, NICE) and the free VA Insomnia Coach (five weeks). Distinct from the first dream because the outcome is getting help without a clinic; flagged as an overlap.

dark-bedroom.title: A bedroom that goes properly dark at night
dark-bedroom.line: When I switch off the lamp, no streetlight or standby glow gets in, and I wake up less groggy.
dark-bedroom.writerNotes: Northwestern's lab study: one night at 100 lux vs 3 lux raised heart rate and insulin resistance. A basic people can reach tonight with curtains or a mask.

noises-stop-waking-me.title: Small noises no longer jolting me awake
noises-stop-waking-me.line: A steady, low sound in my room covers the doors and traffic outside, so I sleep through the little noises.
noises-stop-waking-me.writerNotes: White and pink noise is the common thing people do; the review found weak but mostly positive evidence (pink noise 9 of 11). Kept as a basic; the fix copy should state the weak evidence once.

separate-rooms-both-rest.title: Sleeping in separate rooms so we both rest
separate-rooms-both-rest.line: My partner and I both sleep through the night, even if that means separate rooms some nights.
separate-rooms-both-rest.writerNotes: The copy guide's after-example. AASM survey: over a third of U.S. adults do this. Outcome is both partners resting, with no judgment attached.

snoring-checked-and-treated.title: Knowing whether my snoring is sleep apnea
snoring-checked-and-treated.line: I found out what my snoring means and got it treated, so I wake up clear-headed instead of foggy.
snoring-checked-and-treated.writerNotes: About 23.5 million U.S. adults have undiagnosed apnea; the Apple Watch feature screens for it. Sensitive health topic: the dream names the outcome (an answer and treatment), not a diagnosis.

evenings-free-from-work-messages.title: Evenings free from work messages
evenings-free-from-work-messages.line: When I finish work, I'm actually finished, and my phone stays quiet until morning.
evenings-free-from-work-messages.writerNotes: The copy guide's after-example. Portugal's duty of no contact shows it can be law; teams can also agree it informally, which later fixes can carry.

full-night-between-shifts.title: A full night's sleep between one shift and the next
full-night-between-shifts.line: My schedule always leaves me at least 11 hours off between shifts, so I can get home, sleep a full night, and eat before I go back.
full-night-between-shifts.writerNotes: EU Working Time Directive guarantees 11 consecutive hours of rest. Speaks to shift workers and those on clopening schedules, a group the other dreams miss.

school-starts-after-teens-wake.title: School that starts late enough for my teenager to sleep
school-starts-after-teens-wake.line: My teenager's first class starts at 8:30 or later, so they get up without a fight and sleep about half an hour more.
school-starts-after-teens-wake.writerNotes: Seattle (8:45 start, about 34 more minutes of sleep) and California SB 328 (8:30 for high schools). Written for a parent, since the pain line is first person and parents lose sleep over this too.

no-planes-at-night.title: No planes over my house at night
no-planes-at-night.line: Nothing flies overhead between when I go to bed and when I get up.
no-planes-at-night.writerNotes: The copy guide's after-example. Frankfurt residents won an 11 p.m. to 5 a.m. ban in court.

street-quiet-enough-for-open-window.title: A street quiet enough to sleep with the window open
street-quiet-enough-for-open-window.line: Through traffic and loud motorbikes no longer pass under my window at night, so I can leave it open and still sleep.
street-quiet-enough-for-open-window.writerNotes: Barcelona superblocks residents reported less noise and better sleep; Paris is testing noise radar for loud vehicles. Both are neighborhood-level changes.

clocks-stay-the-same-all-year.title: Clocks that stay the same all year
clocks-stay-the-same-all-year.line: I no longer lose a week of good sleep every spring when the clocks jump forward.
clocks-stay-the-same-all-year.writerNotes: Contested: sleep doctors back permanent standard time, while Congress has debated permanent daylight saving time. The line names the outcome (no switch) without picking a side; fixes should present both directions.

employer-that-rewards-sleep.title: An employer that rewards rest instead of late nights
employer-that-rewards-sleep.line: My workplace treats a full night's sleep as part of doing the job well, and nobody brags about running on five hours.
employer-that-rewards-sleep.writerNotes: Aetna paid for 7-hour nights; Crazy Inc. gave cafeteria points for 6. Both raise privacy questions about tracking staff sleep, so the line describes the culture, not the tracking.

resting-without-guilt.title: Napping on a hard day without feeling guilty
resting-without-guilt.line: When I'm worn out, I lie down for a nap and don't feel I've failed at anything.
resting-without-guilt.writerNotes: The Nap Ministry frames rest as something people are owed, with free group naps in Atlanta. A culture-lens dream about permission to rest, not a sleep disorder.

overlaps.reason: Both end in sleeping well after insomnia therapy; the second differs only in getting it on a phone.
Both describe a workplace that stops eating into the night, one through no messages and one through how rest is valued.
Both protect time off work for sleep; one is about messages, the other about hours between shifts.
Both are quieter nights from transport noise near home, from planes and from road traffic.
Both end with outside noise no longer waking me, one by covering it in my room and one by removing it from the street.
